name: Mayotte

findings.controller: Orange (consortium lead; equipment supplier not stated)
findings.local_actor: FLY-LION3 consortium (Orange, Société Réunionnaise du Radiotéléphone, Comores Câbles)
findings.summary: FLY-LION3, a roughly 400 km submarine cable laid by Orange Marine between Kaweni (Mamoudzou) and Moroni, Comoros, was commissioned in October 2019 by an Orange-led consortium, linking Mayotte onward to the LION2 and EASSy systems.
findings.analyst_inference: Controller convention follows GUF/GLP: MYT is coded as its own territory, so French-company controllers are 'third'; only Mahoran actors are domestic. Wet-plant and terminal-equipment supplier not named in any opened source, so documented owner-operator Orange (France) is treated as controller. All three sources trace to Orange announcements; TelecomTV piece sits in Orange's sponsored channel, coded S4, so only one independent S2 source and not corroborated. Pre-2020; current operation not confirmed in this run, so still_current null. Sources differ on landing date (25 Feb vs 12 Mar 2019).

findings.controller: Information Technology Hosting SAS (ITH), Mayotte-founded operator
findings.financier: Banque des Territoires (equity, ~44%), AFD and Crédit Agricole Mutuel de La Réunion (loans), FEDER, Conseil départemental de Mayotte
findings.summary: ITH's neutral colocation data centre in Mamoudzou, Mayotte's first designed to Tier III (420 kW, about 76-80 racks), opened in October 2022 after a roughly EUR 10m financing closed in November 2020; about 30 clients were reported.

sources.publisher: Caisse des Dépôts / Banque des Territoires

findings.analyst_inference: Building rule: owner-operator ITH is a Mayotte-founded company majority-held by its local founder, so pole domestic; Banque des Territoires (French state group) holds a ~44% minority stake, which is a judgment call reviewers may weigh. Tier 5 because the facility is open with tenants (about 70% of racks taken per Mayotte Hebdo, Oct 2022). Rack count differs by source (76 vs 80). EUR values not converted, so USD null. Post-Chido (Dec 2024) status not checked.

findings.summary: Orange began offering 5G in Mayotte to business customers from 18 October 2023 and was still the only operator doing so in December 2024; SFR said it intended to follow without giving a date.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: the radio-equipment vendor for Orange's Mayotte 5G network is not named, and the equipment rule makes the vendor the controller. Tier 4 because only a business-only service is documented, not consumer rollout at scale.

findings.financier: French State (EUR 1m) and Commune de Mamoudzou
findings.summary: Mamoudzou was expanding a EUR 4.8m municipal video-protection network, with 58 cameras running and a similar number due in a first phase, monitored live by operators for traffic enforcement; no vendor or AI features were reported.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null because no camera, software or integrator vendor is identified; included as a lead for a vendor check. Tier 4 because the expansion is funded and partly installed. EUR values not converted, so USD null.

silicon.null_reason: no dedicated search; no accelerator purchase or export-licence item surfaced in other searches

models.null_reason: one search found no Mayotte government or departmental partnership with any model provider and no local model

research_gaps: Wet-plant and line-terminal equipment supplier of FLY-LION3 (check for HMN Tech), and whether Mayotte has any route other than FLY-LION3 and LION/LION2.

Radio/core equipment vendors of Orange, SFR (SRR) and Only (Free/Axian) in Mayotte, including equipment replaced after Cyclone Chido (Dec 2024), and any Huawei kit under France's 2019 high-risk-vendor regime.
Whether the ITH Tier III data centre survived Cyclone Chido intact and remains operational; any further data-centre projects.
Camera and software vendor for Mamoudzou's video-protection network and any algorithmic features.
